fields.claim_label: The design scorer's composite rank_score did not beat its own strongest single term, the joint Mahalanobis term, on the primary ranking endpoint.
fields.claim_description: STATUS: an observed result from one blind, family-out held-out run of scorer v1.3.0 over 168 held-out families, scored by an evaluator who built neither the scorer nor the benchmark (SCORER-EVALUATION.md:13, :14). The composite beats nearest-neighbour distance (0.875, +0.032) but not the joint term alone, whose own score is 0.883 (SCORER-EVALUATION.md:33, :35, :38). This is a single-run, single-version observation; the dossier gives no figures for other scorer versions. DOES NOT ESTABLISH: that the composite is truly worse than the joint term on the primary endpoint, because the interval for the difference (-0.008, CI -0.020 to 0.002) includes zero; that the other components are useless, since they earn their place on secondary endpoints S4 and S5 which the joint term alone fails (SCORER-EVALUATION.md:43); or that the pattern holds beyond these 168 families. The only significant gap is over all held-out items, where the composite is worse by -0.007 (CI -0.013 to -0.002) (SCORER-EVALUATION.md:36).
fields.evidence_label: Blind held-out comparison of rank_score against nearest-neighbour distance and the joint Mahalanobis term alone, scorer v1.3.0

fields.claim_label: That real held-out organisms score plausible says almost nothing about whether the design scorer works, because negatives score plausible too.
fields.claim_description: Status: an observation from one blind, family-out held-out evaluation (168 held-out families, every scorer version), as recorded in SCORER-EVALUATION.md lines 14 and 45-47; it is a reading of that report, not an independently replicated result. Every version is close to calling everything plausible: 98 to 99.6 % of real organisms are at or above the 0.5 cut, but only 12 to 17 % of negatives fall below it. What this does NOT establish: it does not show that any scorer is useless or wrong, it does not measure discrimination by any other metric, and it does not say how the scorers rank against each other; it only shows that the share of real organisms scoring high is not evidence of a working scorer. The per-family low scorers (locators :183 and :186) are illustrations, not a causal explanation.
fields.evidence_label: Plausibility pass rate for real organisms versus negatives at the 0.5 cut, held-out family-out run
fields.evidence_description: Figures taken from SCORER-EVALUATION.md (locators sim-engine/validate/evaluation/SCORER-EVALUATION.md:14, :45, :46, :47, :183, :186). Real held-out organisms nearly all pass the cut, while few negatives are rejected by it, so the pass rate on real organisms cannot separate a working scorer from one that accepts everything.

fields.claim_label: The design scorer's composite has never beaten its own strongest single term, the joint Mahalanobis term, on the primary ranking endpoint P1.
fields.claim_description: STATUS: this is an observed result, not a theory. It comes from the blind held-out run of scorer version 1.3.0, scored family-out over 168 held-out families (SCORER-EVALUATION.md:14), run by an evaluator who built neither the scorer nor the benchmark; dev results count for nothing (SCORER-EVALUATION.md:13). What was seen: the composite rank_score beats nearest-neighbour distance on P1 at 0.875 (+0.032, CI 0.026 to 0.040; SCORER-EVALUATION.md:33), but against the joint Mahalanobis term used alone the P1 difference is -0.008, CI -0.020 to 0.002, so it is not significantly better on P1 (SCORER-EVALUATION.md:35). Over all held-out items the composite is significantly worse than the joint term alone: -0.007, CI -0.013 to -0.002 (SCORER-EVALUATION.md:36). The joint term alone reaches P1 0.883 and passes all three primary endpoints by itself (SCORER-EVALUATION.md:38). DOES NOT ESTABLISH: (1) that the other components are useless; they earn their place only on secondary endpoints S4 and S5, which the joint term alone fails (SCORER-EVALUATION.md:43). (2) that the composite is worse on P1 specifically; the P1 difference interval spans zero, so P1 alone shows no significant gap either way. (3) anything beyond these 168 families or beyond scorer version 1.3.0; other scorer versions and other family sets are untested by this result. Source locators: sim-engine/validate/evaluation/SCORER-EVALUATION.md:14, :33, :35, :36, :38, :43, :13.

fields.claim_label: That real held-out organisms score plausible says almost nothing about whether the design scorer works, because negatives score plausible too.
fields.claim_description: STATUS: a descriptive finding from one blind, family-out held-out evaluation of every scorer version (168 held-out families; SCORER-EVALUATION.md:14), read from the evaluation write-up; it has not been independently replicated or peer reviewed. The write-up reports that 98 to 99.6 % of real held-out organisms score at or above the 0.5 plausibility cut in every version (SCORER-EVALUATION.md:45), while only 12 to 17 % of negatives score below that same cut (SCORER-EVALUATION.md:46), so every version is close to calling everything plausible (SCORER-EVALUATION.md:47). WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: it does not show that any scorer version is useless or wrong, since a scorer could still rank candidates usefully even with a poorly placed cut; it does not give a better threshold or a discrimination metric; and it says nothing about how negatives were constructed beyond what the locators state. It only shows that the share of real organisms scoring high is not, by itself, evidence of a working scorer.
